changes.after: Keep a copied value after a local variable's block ends.

before: A local variable declared inside braces is visible only within its scope. Code outside that block cannot refer to its name.
For these ordinary local variables, the object’s lifetime ends when its block exits. A saved pointer or reference does not extend that lifetime.
Copying a small integer into an outer variable before the inner block ends gives the outer variable its own surviving value.
Returning a pointer or reference to an ordinary local object leaves a dangling observer after the function exits. Such code may compile but using it is unsafe; it is not a valid runtime experiment.
Expected output or behavior: 7. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Copy a value out of a small block and identify which object survives. Explain why saving an address is not the same as copying the value. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: Scope is the region where you can use a name. A name declared inside a block's braces is not available outside that block.
Lifetime is the time an object exists. The ordinary local variable inner is destroyed when its block ends. Saving a pointer or reference to it would not keep it alive.
Copying inner into saved gives saved its own value. saved was created in the outer block, so it remains available after the inner block ends.
A dangling pointer or reference refers to an object that no longer exists. Returning a reference to an ordinary local variable can create this problem, even if the compiler accepts the code.
The program prints 7. saved receives its own copy of seven while inner is still alive.
After the inner block, saved still exists and inner does not. The output reads saved's value, so it does not need the destroyed object.

after: Scope tells you where a name can be used; lifetime tells you when its object exists.

before.question: Change the final output to inner instead of saved. What happens?
choices: Compilation rejects the name because inner is outside its scope.
It prints 7 because all local names are global.
The inner block automatically runs again.
before.explanation: The copied value remains in saved, but inner’s name is no longer in scope.

after.question: Change the final output to inner instead of saved. What happens?
choices: The compiler rejects inner because its name is outside its scope.
It prints 7 because every local name is available everywhere.
The inner block automatically runs again.
after.explanation: inner's name is only available inside its block. saved holds the copy that can be used afterward.
